title: How do stores decide what goes on sale?
sources: Journal of Consumer Research Price Anchoring

lines.text: When you see a fifty-dollar shirt discounted to twenty-five dollars, are you really getting a great deal?
lines.caps: Are retail store *sales | really saving you *money?

lines.text: Retailers use a psychological mind trick called price anchoring.
The company never intended to sell that shirt for fifty dollars in the first place.
lines.caps: They never *planned | to sell it at full *price

lines.text: By showing you a high original price, your brain anchors to fifty dollars, perceiving twenty-five as a massive win.
lines.caps: Your brain anchors to *50 | making 25 feel like a *steal!

lines.text: Department stores also slash prices to clear warehouse inventory for incoming seasonal collections.
lines.caps: Sales clear old *inventory | to make room for new *stock

lines.text: They often sell loss leaders—like four-dollar rotisserie chickens—at a financial loss just to get you walking past expensive items.
lines.caps: Loss leaders lure you *inside | to buy high-profit *items!

lines.text: Never buy something just because it is on sale; buy it only if you truly need it.
lines.caps: Don't buy the *discount | buy only what you *need!
